authoredSolutions.14: Since \(\rho=\dfrac{R\pi r^{2}}{l}\), \[\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}=\frac{\Delta R}{R}+2\frac{\Delta r}{r}+\frac{\Delta l}{l}=\frac{10}{100}+2\times\frac{0.05}{0.35}+\frac{0.2}{15}.\] This gives \(0.100+0.2857+0.0133=0.399\), i.e. \(39.9\%\). The correct choice is B.

authoredSolutions.18: The figure gives a trolley of mass \(20\ kg\) on the table and a hanging block of weight \(60\ N\) (mass \(6\ kg\)). authoredSolutions.20: With the pattern formed in the focal plane of a lens of focal length \(f\), the linear width of the central maximum is \[W=\frac{2\lambda f}{a}=\frac{2\times6\times10^{-7}\times0.2}{1\times10^{-5}}=2.4\times10^{-2}\ m=24\ mm.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.21: Each side of the hexagon has length \(a=\dfrac{4\pi}{6}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\ m\), and the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side is \[r=\frac{a}{2}\cot 30^{\circ}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\cdot\sqrt3=\frac{a\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{\pi\sqrt3}{3}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt3}\ m.\] Each finite side subtends \(30^{\circ}\) on either side of the foot of the perpendicular, so \[B=6\times\frac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi r}\left(\sin 30^{\circ}+\sin 30^{\circ}\right)=6\times\frac{10^{-7}\times 4\pi\sqrt3}{\pi/\sqrt3}=6\times 12\times10^{-7}=72\times10^{-7}\ T.\] Hence \(x=72\).

authoredSolutions.31: In DNA the base pairing rule is adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine. Reading the given strand ATGCTTCA base by base, A pairs with T, T with A, G with C, C with G, T with A, T with A, C with G and A with T. authoredSolutions.32: The cyanide ion is an ambident nucleophile. \(KCN\) is predominantly ionic, so the free \(CN^{-}\) attacks through the more nucleophilic carbon and gives the alkyl cyanide. \(AgCN\) is largely covalent, so only the nitrogen lone pair is available and the isocyanide is formed. Assertion (A) is therefore correct, but Reason (R) is wrong because \(AgCN\) is covalent, not highly ionic. The answer is option (A).
authoredSolutions.33: In acidic medium dichromate is reduced to \(Cr^{3 +}\): chromium goes from \(+6\) to \(+3\), so two chromium atoms need \(6\) electrons. Balancing oxygen with water gives \(7H_{2}O\), and balancing hydrogen then requires \(14H^{+}\). The half reaction is \[Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2 -}+ 14H^{+}+ 6e^{-}\rightarrow 2Cr^{3 +}+ 7H_{2}O\] so \(X = 14\), \(Y = 6\), \(Z = 7\) and \(A = Cr^{3 +}\), which is option (D).
authoredSolutions.34: In a disproportionation the SAME element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced. In (A) \(Cu^{+}\) goes to \(Cu^{2 +}\) and \(Cu^{0}\), and in (B) \(Mn(+6)\) goes to \(Mn(+7)\) and \(Mn(+4)\) - both qualify. In (C) manganese is only reduced (\(+7 \rightarrow +6\) and \(+4\)) while oxygen is oxidised, so it is an ordinary redox change, not a disproportionation. Reaction (D) is the reverse process, a comproportionation. Hence only (A) and (B), option (A).
authoredSolutions.35: \(F^{-}\), \(Ne\) and \(Na^{+}\) all have \(10\) electrons in the same shells, so the principal quantum number and the electron-electron repulsions are effectively identical. What changes is the nuclear charge (\(Z = 9, 10, 11\)); the larger the nuclear charge the more tightly the same electron cloud is pulled in, so the size falls in the order \(F^{-} > Ne > Na^{+}\). The deciding factor is nuclear charge, option (D).
authoredSolutions.36: The de Broglie relation is \(\lambda = h/p\), so \(\lambda\) is inversely proportional to \(p\) and a plot of \(\lambda\) against \(p\) is a rectangular hyperbola falling steeply and then flattening. The decreasing hyperbolic curve of \(\lambda\) versus \(p\) is option (A).

authoredSolutions.38: \(NH_{3}\) molecules are associated in the liquid state through hydrogen bonding, which \(PH_{3}\) cannot do because phosphorus is not sufficiently electronegative; \(PH_{3}\) is held only by weak van der Waals forces. authoredSolutions.39: \(Cl_{2}\) in the presence of light attacks the side chain of toluene by a free-radical path; with sufficient chlorine the methyl group is converted to the dichloromethyl group, so \(A\) is benzal chloride \(C_{6}H_{5}CHCl_{2}\). A gem-dihalide on hydrolysis with water at \(373\text{ }K\) gives the carbonyl compound, so \(B\) is benzaldehyde. Benzyl chloride would have hydrolysed to benzyl alcohol and benzoyl chloride cannot arise from radical chlorination, so the answer is option (B).
authoredSolutions.40: Aminobenzene is simply the substitutive name for the compound whose common (and retained IUPAC) name is aniline, \(C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2}\). The two names describe one and the same compound, so Statement I is correct and Statement II, which claims they are different compounds, is incorrect. The answer is option (B).
authoredSolutions.41: A homoleptic complex is one in which the metal is bound to only ONE kind of donor group. \(\left\lbrack Ni(CN)_{4} \right\rbrack^{2 -}\) has four identical cyanide ligands and is therefore homoleptic. The other three complexes each carry two different ligands (\(NH_{3}\) together with \(Cl^{-}\)) and are heteroleptic. The answer is option (A).
authoredSolutions.42: Electrophilic attack is easiest on the ring with the greatest electron density. The four compounds are benzene, toluene, chlorobenzene and phenol. The \(-OH\) group of phenol donates its oxygen lone pair into the ring by resonance and is a powerful activating group, far stronger than the weak hyperconjugative release of the methyl group in toluene; chlorine withdraws electrons inductively and deactivates the ring. Phenol, option (D), is attacked most readily.
authoredSolutions.43: In an ionic (polar) reaction the shared pair of a covalent bond leaves entirely with one of the two atoms, generating a cation and an anion; this uneven splitting is heterolytic cleavage. Homolytic cleavage, in which each atom keeps one electron, produces free radicals and is the hallmark of free-radical, not ionic, reactions. Only statement (B) is therefore correct, which is option (C).
authoredSolutions.44: Ionic character grows with the electronegativity difference between the bonded atoms. \(N_{2}\) has two identical atoms so the difference is zero and the bond is purely covalent. The increasing order is \(N_{2} < ClF_{3} < SO_{2} < K_{2}O < LiF\), option (D).
authoredSolutions.45: \(NaCl\) is a strong electrolyte whose limiting van't Hoff factor is \(2\), but at finite concentration interionic attraction makes some ions behave as pairs, so the observed \(i\) is below \(2\). Since \(A\) is the most concentrated and \(C\) the most dilute, \(i_{A} < i_{B} < i_{C}\), option (A).
authoredSolutions.46: In Kjeldahl's method the organic compound is digested with concentrated \(H_{2}SO_{4}\) so that the nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate. \(CuSO_{4}\) (along with \(K_{2}SO_{4}\)) is added only to speed this digestion up; it is not consumed and neither donates nor accepts electrons in the overall change. It therefore acts as a catalytic agent, option (B).
authoredSolutions.47: Potassium hydrogen phthalate is a stable, non-hygroscopic solid of high and accurately known equivalent mass, so it is the classic primary standard against which \(NaOH\) solution (which is hygroscopic and absorbs \(CO_{2}\), and so cannot itself be a primary standard) is standardised. Both statements are correct, option (A).
authoredSolutions.48: An ester is cut back only as far as the aldehyde by the bulky hydride donor DIBAL-H followed by aqueous work-up, so (A) matches (IV). The answer is option (B).
authoredSolutions.49: Free expansion means expansion into a vacuum, so the external pressure is zero and \(w = -p_{ext}\Delta V = 0\). Adiabatic means \(q = 0\). authoredSolutions.51: 2-chlorobutane is \(CH_{3}CHClCH_{2}CH_{3}\). With one chiral centre the number of optical isomers is \(2^{1}= 2\), a pair of enantiomers. The answer is \(2\).
authoredSolutions.52: For \(2H^{+}+ 2e^{-}\rightarrow H_{2}\) the standard potential is zero and \(n = 2\), with reaction quotient \(Q = P_{H_{2}}/\left\lbrack H^{+} \right\rbrack^{2}= 2/1^{2}= 2\). authoredSolutions.53: Taking the salts in turn: \(SrSO_{4}\) white, \(Mg\left( NH_{4} \right)PO_{4}\) white, \(BaCrO_{4}\) yellow, \(Mn(OH)_{2}\) white, \(PbSO_{4}\) white, \(PbCrO_{4}\) yellow, \(AgBr\) pale yellow, \(PbI_{2}\) yellow, \(CaC_{2}O_{4}\) white and the basic iron(III) acetate brownish-red. authoredSolutions.54: Radioactive decay is first order, so the amount left after \(n\) half-lives is \(\left( 1/2 \right)^{n}\) of the original. authoredSolutions.55: Trigonal bipyramidal geometry requires five bond pairs and no lone pair on the central atom. \(PF_{5}\), \(PCl_{5}\) and \(Fe(CO)_{5}\) all satisfy this. \(BrF_{5}\) has five bond pairs plus one lone pair and is square pyramidal, \(\left\lbrack PtCl_{4} \right\rbrack^{2 -}\) is square planar, and \(BF_{3}\) is trigonal planar. authoredSolutions.56: The five groups shown are \(-COOCH_{3}\), \(-NHCOCH_{3}\), \(-NHCH_{3}\), \(-CN\) and \(-OCH_{3}\). The number of deactivating groups is \(2\).
authoredSolutions.57: The most negative oxidation number an atom can reach is fixed by how many electrons it needs to complete its octet. If that lowest oxidation number is \(-2\), the atom gains two electrons to reach eight, so it already holds \(8 - 2 = 6\) electrons in its valence shell (a group 16 element, consistent with the formula \(A_{2}B\)). The answer is \(6\).
authoredSolutions.58: An amphoteric oxide dissolves in both acid and alkali.
